Submit only the root repository link (`https://github.com//`) through the Classroom assignment.” # Build plan for the IT access-request intake This plan implements `planning/spec.md` R-01–R-105 using the four source documents and all 20 request messages. Only this plan is being written now. All module paths, commands, tests, fixtures and outputs below are proposed future work; none is reported as implemented, run or passing. Implementation choices below are choices for satisfying the spec, not new source requirements. No application code, tests, fixtures, dependency changes, outputs, commits or submissions belong to this planning task. ## Choices - **Runtime:** Python 3.11 or later, standard-library `unittest`, `sqlite3`, `argparse`, hashing and HTTP transport, with `jsonschema` declared in `pyproject.toml` and dependencies locked in `uv.lock`; this fits the supplied Python test harness and keeps deployment small. - **Interface:** a CLI invoked as `python3 -m intake`, with `run`, `queue`, `resume`, `retry`, `history`, `export` and `accuracy` subcommands; separate invocations can inspect committed results while intake continues, and the same commands support handover and recovery. - **Tests:** `env -u API_KEY python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, plus the spec’s individual `-k test_rNN_contract` filters; tests use temporary directories/databases, deterministic scripted responses and a blocked real network, so no test or build step needs a real API_KEY. - **Model provider:** a provider interface with a scripted mock and a configurable OpenAI Responses adapter over an injected HTTPS JSON transport; request model ID, endpoint, request settings and timeout are explicit configuration, with production authentication read only from API_KEY and no credential stored in configuration fingerprints. Verify the exact supported request/response fields against current official provider documentation before implementation, record the chosen model ID/configuration in README and evidence, and test the real adapter entirely through intercepted transport rather than a live call. The initial supported shared-operation arrangement is multiple CLI processes on one host using one local SQLite database; filesystem/network-share and multi-host database behavior are outside this arrangement and will be documented rather than claimed as tested. SQLite is the authoritative current/history store. Immutable attempts and source revisions are retained separately from current projections, with transactional current-record pointers. Extractions and queue views read the same committed attempt. Export both deliverables from one read snapshot into an immutable generation and expose the generation through one atomic directory reference, so a failed publication cannot expose a half-written generation; document the local-filesystem assumption. An operator reading multiple files across a publication switch must pin one generation. Interrupted workers are recovered through explicit resume with persisted work state and expiring claims; expired workers cannot overwrite a newer claim’s result. Bounded configurable worker concurrency, request timeouts and retry scheduling prevent one slow/rate-limited document from blocking unrelated work; exact tuning is documented as a limit, not a promised throughput. Only successful, validated extraction results are reusable. Retry explicitly bypasses reuse for the selected document. Configuration identity includes producing provider/model/request settings, prompt and schema versions, and policy version; keep the actual nonsecret configuration alongside the identity. A policy-only change may reroute a retained valid extraction into a new attributed attempt; a failed current attempt is retried explicitly rather than silently replaced by historical success. An unchanged source byte hash distinguishes source identity from changes to producing settings. The latest accepted ingestion revision controls the current pointer; an older in-flight response can remain in history but cannot replace that revision. Order revisions by recorded ingestion sequence, since export timestamps are metadata and no cross-batch source ordering authority is specified. Business-purpose prose and issue prose have no source-mandated exact wording. Fixtures record supported purpose facts and source quotes, while checking that the actual purpose expresses those facts without unsupported additions. The strict scalar metric compares the 11 non-purpose scalar fields, including nulls; purpose, issues and quote support receive separate checks/reports. This is a declared measurement choice, not a new application acceptance rule or a required accuracy score. The brief’s unspecified performance thresholds and issue vocabulary remain unspecified. ## Steps, in build order Each numbered step starts by writing its owned tests and observing a failure for the intended missing behavior; collection errors, zero discovered tests and unexpected setup failures are not a meaningful red result. Implement just enough to make those tests pass, then run the complete mock suite. Each named test belongs to exactly one step; later steps may rerun it without taking ownership. It prepares requests for people; a named manager is a contact, and successful intake never means approval. 24:python3 -m intake queue --db var/demo.sqlite --include-pending 27:python3 -m intake history --db var/demo.sqlite --document IT-010.json 31:`run` accepts a directory or one exported JSON file. `queue` reads committed current outcomes even while another CLI process is preparing other documents; `--include-pending` also shows pending/running work without pretending it has a completed business status. `history` retains every attempt with its source bytes/hash, configuration, policy identity and outcome. Inputs absent from a later batch remain present. A corrected message or relevant producing-settings change creates a new attempt; `--refresh` explicitly forces one. Explicit retry bypasses reuse, and a failed retry becomes the current error while previous success remains identifiable in history. 33:Run recovery with `resume` after a crash or deployment interruption. It continues pending work and running work whose claim expired; the default claim lifetime is request timeout + 5 seconds. An active claim is left alone. Resume reconstructs settings per document, supports parallel progress and refreshes work if prompt/schema/policy versions changed. An older or expired worker token cannot replace a newer claim's result. Pending work with changed settings is marked superseded in history rather than mislabelled as produced under those earlier settings. 59:## Shared operation, history and publication limits 61:Support is for multiple CLI processes on one host sharing one local SQLite database and local output directory; multi-host and network-share locking are not supported. Transactions keep claims/current pointers coherent. Immutable attempts are separate from current outputs. The latest accepted ingestion order controls the current source revision; export timestamps are display metadata. A late response can be retained in earlier history but cannot replace a newer current document revision. 63:Exports are generated from one committed snapshot. An advisory publisher lock serializes snapshot-to-publication work. `deliverables/current` atomically selects an immutable `.generations/` directory, and `extractions.jsonl`/`queue.json` are stable links through it. A reader inspecting both files during concurrent publication must resolve and pin `current` once, then read both files in that directory. Abandoned unpublished generations may remain on disk after interruption; retain them for investigation. Export again to publish the latest database state. The database is authoritative between exports.

content.text: The plan selects a CLI and has functional tests for intake, queue inspection, and recovery. I found no accessibility acceptance checks for those workflows. I’ll add CLI-specific checks and keep web requirements conditional on a web interface being delivered.

# AI Full Stack Challenge — IT Access Requests

## The task
Northstar Labs receives access requests as free-text messages. Build a small runnable application that uses a language model to turn those messages into structured records and a review queue for the IT team. The supplied company, people and requests are fictional.

Read docs/requirements.md for the operating context and required behavior, materials/office-policy.md for review rules, and snapshot.schema.json for the record format. The 20 JSON exports in materials/requests/ are your starting data. Choose an interface suited to the IT team: a CLI, service or web application. Operators should be able to start intake, inspect completed results while other requests are pending, and resume unfinished work through the documented interface.

## What to submit
This brief ships as CHALLENGE.md; the README.md below is yours to write.

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| README.md | Setup, supported runtime/provider, exact intake/test/accuracy-check commands, environment-variable names, and how to inspect the queue |
| Source code and dependency lockfile | Runnable application, extraction prompt, schema and model request configuration |
| deliverables/extractions.jsonl | One current record per message: document_id, source_sha256, extraction (schema-conforming object, or null on error), status, owner, next_action, error (null on success), and response_source (`mock`, or the provider and model ID that produced the record) |
| deliverables/queue.json | The review queue linked to extraction records by document_id |
| deliverables/accuracy.md | Source-derived expected fields for the 20 supplied messages and one paraphrase you author; the field-comparison procedure, exact-match counting/denominator rules, factual-error reporting and model/configuration; distinguish mocked examples from any optional live observations |
| deliverables/request-evidence.json | Credential-redacted example model request showing the model ID and configuration used, plus the implemented response handling |
| deliverables/verification.md | Verification commands and assertions, their intended comparisons, operating limits, and any observed results or repairs clearly identified as such |
| Coding-session capture | Session record paired with the submitted commit, collected through the facilitator's capture setup |

## Submission
Commit and push the application, outputs and session capture to your repository's default branch. Submit only the root repository link (`https://github.com/<your-account>/<repository>`) through the Classroom assignment. The facilitator supplies the assignment and capture instructions.

Submit the implemented provider integration and source-grounded validation procedure. Use mocked responses for reproducible development examples, and label each recorded observation with its configuration and whether it used a mock or provider response. The committed deliverables may come from mocked or provider responses; each record's response_source says which.
# Requirements — IT Access Requests

## Operating context

Northstar Labs is a fictional multinational company with approximately 5,000 employees across offices in Asia, Europe and North America. Its regional IT teams share responsibility for preparing access requests for human review. They receive free-text messages through email, chat and the service portal, then work from JSON exports of those messages.

### Workload and the review day

On an ordinary business day, the company receives around 200–400 request messages. A coordinated onboarding or acquisition can bring roughly 2,000 messages into the morning's intake. The supplied 20 exports are a representative sample of message types; the application will also receive other messages in the same export format.

Reviewers begin work at different local times. They want to start on requests that are ready while the rest of the intake is still being prepared. A slow response for one message should leave the rest of their work available. Model access is shared with other internal tools, and the available request rate and response time can vary.

### Shared operations

Regional operators work against the same intake and review records. Their working hours overlap, and two operators may start processing around the same time. Each expects their work to leave a coherent current queue and a trustworthy record of earlier activity.

The application may be stopped during a deployment or interrupted by a service outage. When an operator returns, they need to distinguish completed work from unfinished work and continue from the recorded state. Reviewers rely on the queue and the supporting extraction records agreeing about the same source version.

### Updates and follow-up

Exports arrive throughout the day. A later export may repeat an unchanged document or replace its contents with a corrected or expanded message. An export batch contains new or updated documents; absence from a later batch does not withdraw an earlier request. Withdrawal is expressed in the message and handled under the office policy.

Operators need the current view to reflect the latest processed source and to retain earlier results for follow-up. If a new processing attempt fails, they need to see that failure and identify any older result as belonging to its earlier attempt and source version.

The team periodically changes model configuration and updates its review policy. When such a change affects how records are produced or routed, operators need to refresh the affected results and understand which settings and policy version produced the records they are using.

### Service interruptions and handover

The model service sometimes responds slowly, limits requests or becomes temporarily unavailable. IT staff need to locate affected messages, understand what remains pending and resume processing without losing completed work. Other messages may contain incomplete or conflicting information that needs clarification from the requester.

The original developer and the next operator may be in different offices. The operator will use the repository's setup instructions, configuration guidance and commands to prepare an intake, inspect the queue and follow up on failures. Explain the operating assumptions and limits of your implementation so that this handover is practical.

## Record and review behavior
- Use a language model to extract the request details into records that conform to snapshot.schema.json.
- Validate response structure and completion status before using extracted data. Preserve exact supporting quotes and represent uncertain fields as null with an explanatory issue.
- Use message content as the source of business facts. Preserve missing values, conflicting alternatives and explicit corrections according to the policy. Keep document identity distinct from the request ID stated in the message.
- Apply the supplied review policy and display each request's status, owner and next action. Approval decisions belong to the named human reviewers.
- Record input filenames and SHA-256 hashes. Reuse results when the source and relevant processing settings are unchanged, refresh affected results when those inputs or settings change, and retain earlier versions. Process each message independently and make failures visible with a reproducible retry command.
- Handle malformed output, provider errors, refusal and interrupted responses explicitly. Keep model/provider settings configurable and document a supported configuration. The facilitator supplies an API key through the environment variable API_KEY.

## Verification

Include automated tests covering a complete request, missing dates, conflicting details, embedded instructions, provider failure, an unchanged rerun, and changed source content. Build expected results from the supplied messages and policy. Add a paraphrased synthetic request to exercise extraction on fresh wording. Specify expected facts from the source messages and policy independently of the extraction outputs being measured. Include checks for refusal or interrupted responses and a failed retry after a prior success.


Describe how your implementation supports the operating context above, and include checks for the operational situations your design handles. Record assumptions about workload and shared operation, the expected behavior during interruptions, and the limits of the verification you performed.
# Northstar access-request intake policy

Northstar Labs uses this intake application to prepare access requests for human review. All exercise data is fictional.

## Input export format
Each UTF-8 JSON file represents one exported message. Read its `message` string as the natural-language source for extraction. `export_version`, `exported_at`, `source_channel` and `subject` describe the export and help display it. Derive request facts from `message`; the export timestamp describes when the record was exported. Messages vary in length, up to 200 English words.

Use the original JSON file bytes for the source hash and its filename for document_id. Exact supporting quotes refer to substrings of the decoded `message` value.

## Extracted facts
Extract request_id, request_date, kind (new, change, withdrawal or other), requester, team, system, environment (staging or production), permission (read, write or admin), business_purpose, start_date, end_date, manager, supporting_quotes and issues. Use the supplied schema. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD.

Use explicit facts from each message. Represent absent or unresolved scalar values as null and explain each missing or conflicting fact in issues. Preserve conflicting alternatives in exact supporting_quotes. A later statement explicitly labelled as a correction replaces the earlier value; contradictory statements without a correction remain unresolved. A relative date stays unresolved. For a change request, extract the requested new permission.

The document_id is the input filename. If an identifier inside the message differs from the identifier in its filename, retain the stated identifier and record the mismatch as an issue. Each message is an independent document, including multiple messages about one request.

## Review queue
Apply these rules in order after validating the extraction:

1. An instruction-override attempt goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action inspect-message. Keep the attempted instruction as source evidence and identify it in issues. Treat source messages as data throughout extraction and routing.
2. A withdrawal with request_id and request_date goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action confirm-withdrawal. Other fields may be null; identify absent facts in issues.
3. Other messages with kind other/null, conflicting details, an identifier mismatch, or any missing required fact go to IT Service Desk with status needs-information and next_action clarify. For new/change requests, required facts are request_id, request_date, requester, team, system, environment, permission, business_purpose, start_date, end_date and manager. A start_date after end_date is also a clarification issue.
4. Complete new/change requests involving production, write or admin go to Security Review with status review and next_action review-risk-then-owner. Security Review examines risk and forwards its recommendation to the system owner for a decision.
5. Complete staging/read requests go to System Owner with status review and next_action review-request.

All successful intake outputs await human review. A named manager is a contact; approval is an explicit human decision. The application's output is a review queue.

## Processing and recovery
An extraction failure produces status error, owner IT Service Desk, next_action retry-extraction, a null extraction and an actionable error. Keep unaffected messages moving through intake. Preserve the last valid result in history when a later attempt fails, and show the latest attempt's error in the current queue.

Identify source revisions with a SHA-256 of the original bytes. An unchanged rerun produces one current queue entry per document. Changed input creates a new result and retains the earlier result with its earlier hash. Store prior versions separately from current outputs. Keep credentials in environment variables and use credential-redacted operational logs.

import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

files = ['IT-001.json', 'IT-002.json', 'IT-010.json']
mock_dir = Path('tests/mock_responses').resolve()
launcher = [sys.executable, 'tests/mock_worker.py']
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='intake-step12-review-') as temp:
    work = Path(temp)
    source, gates, output = (work / name for name in ('input', 'gates', 'output'))
    source.mkdir()
    gates.mkdir()
    for name in files:
        shutil.copyfile(Path('materials/requests') / name, source / name)
    script = work / 'initial.json'
    script.write_text(json.dumps(dict(zip(files, [['blocked-file.json'], [files[1]], ['provider-error.json']]))))
    db = work / 'intake.sqlite'
    db_option = ['--db', str(db)]
    mock_options = ['--provider', 'mock', '--responses', str(mock_dir), '--script', str(script), '--mock-gates', str(gates)]
    def cli(*args, expected=0):
        result = subprocess.run(launcher + list(args), capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=12)
        assert result.returncode == expected, result
        return json.loads(result.stdout)
    def queue():
        return {r['document_id']: r for r in cli('queue', *db_option, '--include-pending')}
    def routing(row):
        return row['owner'], row['status'], row['next_action']
    worker = subprocess.Popen(launcher + ['run', '--input', str(source), *db_option, *mock_options, '--timeout', '12'], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    try:
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 6
        first = {}
        while time.monotonic() < deadline and worker.poll() is None:
            if (gates / 'entered').exists():
                first = queue()
                if first[files[1]].get('status') == 'review' and first[files[2]].get('status') == 'error':
                    break
            time.sleep(0.05)
        else:
            raise AssertionError(first)
        assert first[files[0]]['work_state'] == 'running'
        assert routing(first[files[1]]) == ('Security Review', 'review', 'review-risk-then-owner')
        assert routing(first[files[2]]) == ('IT Service Desk', 'error', 'retry-extraction')
        worker.terminate()
        worker.communicate(timeout=5)
        with sqlite3.connect(db) as conn:
            conn.execute("UPDATE attempts SET expires=0 WHERE state='running'")
        (gates / 'release').touch()
        cli('resume', *db_option, *mock_options, expected=1)
        resumed = queue()
        assert routing(resumed[files[0]]) == ('System Owner', 'review', 'review-request')
        assert resumed[files[1]] == first[files[1]]
        retry = shlex.split(first[files[2]]['retry_command'])
        assert retry[:3] == ['python3', '-m', 'intake']
        cli(*retry[3:], '--script', str(mock_dir / 'manifest.json'))
        assert routing(queue()[files[2]]) == ('IT Service Desk', 'needs-information', 'clarify')
        assert len(cli('history', *db_option, '--document', files[2])) == 2
        cli('export', *db_option, '--output', str(output))
        assert (output / 'queue.json').exists() and (output / 'extractions.jsonl').exists()
        print('Mock baseline passed: mixed queue states, interrupted resume, retry with explicit recovery manifest, history, and export.')
    finally:
        if worker.poll() is None:
            worker.terminate()
            worker.communicate(timeout=5)

"""Documented operator CLI. Mock mode does not touch credential configuration."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys
from .export import publish
from .extract import ResponsesProvider
from .providers import MockProvider
from .runner import Runner
from .source import load
from .store import Store


def parser():
    result = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    commands = result.add_subparsers(dest='command', required=True)
    for command in ['run', 'queue', 'resume', 'retry', 'history', 'export']:
        sub = commands.add_parser(command)
        sub.add_argument('--db', default='var/intake.sqlite')
        if command in ('run', 'resume', 'retry'):
            sub.add_argument('--provider', choices=['mock', 'openai'])
            sub.add_argument('--responses')
            sub.add_argument('--script')
            sub.add_argument('--mock-gates')
            sub.add_argument('--model')
            sub.add_argument('--endpoint')
            sub.add_argument('--timeout', type=float)
            sub.add_argument('--max-output-tokens', type=int)
            sub.add_argument('--workers', type=int, default=4)
            sub.add_argument('--max-retries', type=int, default=0)
            sub.add_argument('--retry-delay', type=float, default=1)
            sub.add_argument('--output')
        if command == 'run':
            sub.add_argument('--input', required=True)
            sub.add_argument('--refresh', action='store_true')
        if command in ('history', 'retry'):
            sub.add_argument('--document', required=True)
        if command == 'queue':
            sub.add_argument('--include-pending', action='store_true')
        if command == 'export':
            sub.add_argument('--output', required=True)
    accuracy = commands.add_parser('accuracy')
    accuracy.add_argument('--input', required=True)
    accuracy.add_argument('--synthetic')
    accuracy.add_argument('--expected', required=True)
    accuracy.add_argument('--responses', default='tests/mock_responses')
    accuracy.add_argument('--provider', choices=['mock', 'openai'], default='mock')
    accuracy.add_argument('--model')
    accuracy.add_argument('--output', required=True)
    return result


def make_runner(args, store, prior_override=None):
    prior = {}
    if args.command == 'retry':
        history = store.history(args.document)
        if history:
            prior = history[-1]['settings']
    elif args.command == 'resume' and store.pending():
        prior = store.pending()[0]['settings']
    if prior_override is not None:
        prior = prior_override
    provider_name = args.provider or ('openai' if prior.get('provider', '').startswith('openai/') else 'mock')
    timeout = args.timeout if args.timeout is not None else prior.get('timeout', 30)
    config = {}
    if provider_name == 'mock':
        root = Path(args.responses or prior.get('mock_responses', 'tests/mock_responses')).resolve()
        script = Path(args.script or prior.get('mock_script', root / 'manifest.json')).resolve()
        provider = MockProvider(root, json.loads(script.read_text()))
        config.update(mock_script=str(script), mock_script_sha256=hashlib.sha256(script.read_bytes()).hexdigest())
        gates = args.mock_gates or prior.get('mock_gates')
        if gates:
            config['mock_gates'] = str(Path(gates).resolve())
    else:
        model = args.model or prior.get('model')
        if not model:
            raise ValueError('--model is required for provider=openai')
        provider = ResponsesProvider(model=model, endpoint=args.endpoint or prior.get('endpoint') or 'https://api.openai.com/v1/responses',
                                     timeout=timeout, max_output_tokens=args.max_output_tokens or prior.get('max_output_tokens', 4096))
    return Runner(store, provider, workers=args.workers, timeout=timeout, max_retries=args.max_retries,
                  retry_delay=args.retry_delay, config=config)


def main(argv=None):
    args = parser().parse_args(argv)
    try:
        if args.command == 'accuracy':
            from .accuracy import run_accuracy
            if args.provider == 'openai' and not args.model:
                raise ValueError('--model is required for provider=openai')
            provider = MockProvider(args.responses) if args.provider == 'mock' else ResponsesProvider(args.model)
            comparison = run_accuracy(args.input, args.synthetic, args.expected, provider, args.output)
            print(json.dumps({'matches': comparison['matches'], 'denominator': comparison['denominator']}))
            return 0 if comparison['matches'] == comparison['denominator'] and not comparison['duplicates'] and not comparison['unexpected'] and not comparison['evidence_errors'] and not comparison['routing_errors'] else 1
        store = Store(args.db)
        if args.command == 'queue':
            print(json.dumps(store.current(args.include_pending), indent=2)); return 0
        if args.command == 'history':
            print(json.dumps(store.history(args.document), indent=2)); return 0
        if args.command == 'export':
            print(json.dumps({'generation': str(publish(store, args.output))})); return 0
        runner = make_runner(args, store)
        if args.command == 'run':
            source = Path(args.input)
            paths = [source] if source.is_file() else sorted(source.glob('*.json'))
            if not paths:
                raise ValueError('input contains no JSON exports')
            runner.run([load(path) for path in paths], force=args.refresh)
        elif args.command == 'resume':
            # Reconstruct producing settings per document rather than borrowing the
            # first pending document's model, endpoint or mock script for all work.
            from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
            def resume_one(pending):
                make_runner(args, store, pending['settings']).resume(attempts=[pending['id']])
            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.workers) as pool:
                list(pool.map(resume_one, store.pending()))
        else:
            runner.retry(args.document)
        if args.output:
            publish(store, args.output)
        rows = store.current(include_pending=True)
        errors = sum(row.get('status') == 'error' for row in rows)
        print(json.dumps({'documents': len(rows), 'errors': errors,
                          'pending': sum(row['work_state'] in ('pending', 'running') for row in rows)}))
        return 1 if errors else 0
    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
        # Do not print untrusted provider bodies, extracted values or credentials.
        print(f'{type(exc).__name__}: command failed; inspect paths, source format and documented configuration', file=sys.stderr)
        return 2


if __name__ == '__main__':
    raise SystemExit(main())
"""Source-oracle comparison, deliberately separate from mock provider replies."""
from collections import Counter
import json
from pathlib import Path
from .extract import prepare
from .policy import route
from .source import load
from .validation import SCHEMA, validate

FIELDS = [key for key in SCHEMA['required'] if key not in ('business_purpose', 'supporting_quotes', 'issues')]


def compare(expected, measured, documents):
    counts = Counter(row['document_id'] for row in measured)
    indexed = {row['document_id']: row for row in measured}
    result = {'matches': 0, 'denominator': len(expected) * len(FIELDS), 'factual_errors': [],
              'missing': sorted(set(expected) - set(counts)),
              'duplicates': sorted(name for name, count in counts.items() if count != 1),
              'unexpected': sorted(set(counts) - set(expected)), 'evidence_errors': [], 'purpose_reviews': [],
              'routing_errors': [], 'by_field': {key: {'matches': 0, 'denominator': len(expected)} for key in FIELDS}, 'by_case': []}
    for name, oracle in sorted(expected.items()):
        row = indexed.get(name)
        actual = row.get('extraction') if row and counts[name] == 1 else None
        actual = actual if isinstance(actual, dict) and not row.get('error') else None
        for field in ['owner', 'status', 'next_action']:
            if row is None or row.get(field) != oracle[field]:
                result['routing_errors'].append({'document_id': name, 'field': field, 'expected': oracle[field], 'actual': row.get(field) if row else None})
        matched = 0
        for field in FIELDS:
            wanted = oracle['fields'][field]
            if actual is not None and field in actual and actual[field] == wanted:
                matched += 1
                result['by_field'][field]['matches'] += 1
            else:
                result['factual_errors'].append({'document_id': name, 'field': field, 'expected': wanted,
                                                  'actual': actual.get(field) if actual else None,
                                                  'reason': 'different or unavailable extraction'})
        result['matches'] += matched
        result['by_case'].append({'document_id': name, 'matches': matched, 'denominator': len(FIELDS)})
        if actual is not None:
            try:
                validate(documents[name], actual)
            except ValueError:
                result['evidence_errors'].append({'document_id': name, 'error': 'schema, issue or exact-quote/date-grounding check failed'})
            purpose = actual.get('business_purpose')
            if purpose and purpose not in documents[name]['message']:
                result['purpose_reviews'].append({'document_id': name, 'actual': purpose, 'source_evidence': oracle['purpose_evidence'],
                                                  'review': 'not a literal source span; review semantic support and unsupported additions manually; this is not an automatic factual-error finding'})
        else:
            result['evidence_errors'].append({'document_id': name, 'error': 'no unique valid extraction to check'})
    return result


def render(result, expected, measured):
    configurations = []
    for row in measured:
        config = {'response_source': row['response_source'], 'settings': row.get('settings', {})}
        if config not in configurations:
            configurations.append(config)
    text = '# Accuracy check\n\n'
    text += f"Exact scalar comparisons: **{result['matches']}/{result['denominator']}**.\n\n"
    text += ('This report uses source-derived expectations authored before extraction. Mock observations measure pipeline handling, not live model accuracy. '
             'No live model call or live accuracy observation is claimed.\n\n'
             'Compare the 11 non-purpose scalar fields exactly, case-sensitively, including nulls; no normalization is applied. '
             'The denominator is expected cases × 11, normally 21 × 11 = 231. Missing/error or duplicate-case extractions count as 11 mismatches. '
             'Unexpected cases are reported separately and do not enlarge the denominator. Purpose, issues and exact evidence are separate checks, not hidden scalar successes. '
             'A faithful paraphrase of purpose does not fail solely because it differs from a canned sentence. Nonliteral purpose text requires manual source review; '
             'this checker cannot prove semantic support or attack resistance. No score threshold is specified.\n\n')
    text += 'Producing configuration and origin:\n\n```json\n' + json.dumps(configurations, indent=2) + '\n```\n\n'
    text += '| Document | Exact scalar matches |\n|---|---|\n'
    for case in result['by_case']:
        text += f"| {case['document_id']} | {case['matches']}/{case['denominator']} |\n"
    text += '\n| Field | Matches |\n|---|---|\n'
    for field, values in result['by_field'].items():
        text += f"| {field} | {values['matches']}/{values['denominator']} |\n"
    text += '\nExpected facts and exact source evidence (supplied messages plus the authored synthetic input):\n\n'
    for name, oracle in sorted(expected.items()):
        text += f"- **{name}**, `{oracle['source']}` /message: “" + oracle['source_quote'].replace('\n', '<br>') + '”\n'
        text += '  Expected fields: `' + json.dumps(oracle['fields'], ensure_ascii=False) + '`; '
        text += f"owner={oracle['owner']}, status={oracle['status']}, next_action={oracle['next_action']}.\n"
    policy = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'materials/office-policy.md'
    text += '\nRouting expectations derive from `materials/office-policy.md` § Review queue:\n\n'
    for line in policy.read_text().splitlines():
        if line[:2] in ('1.', '2.', '3.', '4.', '5.'):
            text += '> ' + line + '\n\n'
    text += 'Comparison findings and factual-error reporting:\n\n```json\n' + json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n```\n'
    return text


def run_accuracy(input_path, synthetic, expected_path, provider, output):
    inputs = Path(input_path)
    paths = [inputs] if inputs.is_file() else sorted(inputs.glob('*.json'))
    if synthetic:
        paths.append(Path(synthetic))
    expected = {path.name: json.loads(path.read_text()) for path in sorted(Path(expected_path).glob('*.json'))}
    documents = {path.name: load(path) for path in paths}
    measured = []
    for path in paths:
        doc = documents[path.name]
        try:
            result = prepare(doc, provider)
            result.update(route(doc, result['extraction']), error=None)
        except ValueError:
            result = {'extraction': None, 'error': 'extraction failed during accuracy check', 'response_source': provider.response_source}
        measured.append(dict(result, document_id=doc['document_id'], source_sha256=doc['source_sha256']))
    comparison = compare(expected, measured, documents)
    output = Path(output)

    output.write_text(render(comparison, expected, measured))
    output.with_suffix('.json').write_text(json.dumps(comparison, indent=2) + '\n')
    return comparison

class Runner:
    def __init__(self, store, provider, workers=4, timeout=30, max_retries=0,
                 retry_delay=1, clock=time.time, sleep=time.sleep, config=None):
        if workers < 1 or timeout <= 0 or max_retries < 0 or retry_delay < 0:
            raise ValueError('invalid worker, timeout or retry configuration')
        self.store, self.provider = store, provider
        self.workers, self.timeout = workers, timeout
        self.max_retries, self.retry_delay = max_retries, retry_delay
        self.clock, self.sleep = clock, sleep
        self.config = settings(provider, config)
        self.config['timeout'] = timeout
        if hasattr(provider, 'root'):
            self.config['mock_responses'] = str(provider.root.resolve())

    def run(self, documents, force=False):
        attempts = [self.store.begin(doc, self.config, force) for doc in documents]
        self._execute([a for a in attempts if a is not None])
        return self.store.current()

    def _execute(self, attempts):
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=self.workers) as pool:
            list(pool.map(self._work, dict.fromkeys(attempts)))

    def retry_command(self, document_id):
        args = ['python3', '-m', 'intake', 'retry', '--db', self.store.path, '--document', document_id]
        if self.provider.response_source == 'mock':
            args += ['--provider', 'mock', '--responses', str(self.provider.root.resolve())]
        return shlex.join(args)

    def _work(self, attempt):
        row = self.store.get(attempt)
        if not row:
            return
        delay = row['not_before'] - self.clock()
        if delay > 0:
            self.sleep(delay)
        while True:
            token = self.store.claim(attempt, now=self.clock(), lease=self.timeout + 5)
            if not token:
                return
            row = self.store.get(attempt)
            doc = row['document']
            try:
                # Use the persisted producing settings when resuming recorded work.
                prepared = prepare(doc, self.provider, row['settings'])
                result = dict(prepared, **route(doc, prepared['extraction']), error=None)
                result['settings'] = row['settings']
            except Exception as exc:
                if isinstance(exc, ProviderError) and exc.retryable and row['tries'] <= self.max_retries:
                    delay = self.retry_delay * (2 ** (row['tries'] - 1))
                    if not self.store.defer(attempt, token, self.clock() + delay):
                        return
                    self.sleep(delay)
                    continue
                message = str(exc).lower()
                category = 'provider-error' if isinstance(exc, ProviderError) else 'invalid-response'
                for word in ['refusal', 'incomplete', 'malformed', 'structure', 'quote']:
                    if word in message:
                        category = word
                        break
                result = {'extraction': None, 'status': 'error', 'owner': 'IT Service Desk',
                          'next_action': 'retry-extraction', 'error': f'{category}: extraction failed; inspect source and recorded provider settings, then retry',
                          'error_type': category, 'retry_command': self.retry_command(doc['document_id']),
                          'response_source': self.provider.response_source, 'settings': row['settings']}
            self.store.finish(attempt, result, token=token, now=self.clock())
            return

    def resume(self, attempts=None):
        rows = self.store.pending()
        if attempts is not None:
            rows = [row for row in rows if row['id'] in attempts]
        work = []

from html import escape
from html.parser import HTMLParser
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import markdown

repo, out = map(Path, sys.argv[1:])
out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

class Audit(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.headings = []
        self.table_headers = 0
        self.bad_links = []
        self.links = 0
        self.in_link = False
        self.link_text = ''
        self.media = 0

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        attrs = dict(attrs)
        if tag in {'h1', 'h2', 'h3', 'h4', 'h5', 'h6'}:
            self.headings.append(int(tag[1]))
        if tag == 'th':
            self.table_headers += 1
        if tag == 'a':
            self.in_link = True
            self.link_text = ''
            self.links += 1
            if not attrs.get('href'):
                self.bad_links.append('missing href')
        if tag in {'img', 'audio', 'video'}:
            self.media += 1

    def handle_data(self, data):
        if self.in_link:
            self.link_text += data

    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag == 'a':
            if not self.link_text.strip():
                self.bad_links.append('empty link name')
            self.in_link = False

for relative in ('README.md', 'deliverables/accuracy.md', 'deliverables/verification.md'):

    audit = Audit()

    assert audit.headings[0] == 1 and audit.headings.count(1) == 1
    assert all(new <= old + 1 for old, new in zip(audit.headings, audit.headings[1:]))

        keycode, mods = self._lastKeyCodeAndModifiers()

    def treatEventAsCommand(self, event):
        if event.source != focus_manager.getManager().get_locus_of_focus():
            return False

        if event.type.startswith("object:text-changed:insert") and event.any_data.strip():
            # To let default script handle presentation.
            if self.lastInputEventWasPaste():
                return False

            if event.any_data.count("\n~"):
                return False

            keyString, mods = self.lastKeyAndModifiers()
            if keyString in ["Return", "Tab", "space", " "]:
                return re.search(r"[^\d\s]", event.any_data)
            if mods & keybindings.ALT_MODIFIER_MASK:
                return True
            if self.lastInputEventWasPrintableKey():
                return len(event.any_data) > 1
            if AXText.get_caret_offset(event.source) == event.detail1 + event.detail2:
                return True

        return False

    def treatEventAsNoise(self, event):
        if self.lastInputEventWasCommand():

        if event.type.startswith("object:text-changed:delete") and event.any_data.strip():
            keyString, mods = self.lastKeyAndModifiers()
            if keyString in ["Return", "Tab", "space", " "]:
                return True
            if mods & keybindings.ALT_MODIFIER_MASK:
                return True
            if len(event.any_data) > 1 and self.lastInputEventWasPrintableKey():
                return True

# Espeak mbrola output module is based on the generic plugin for Speech
# Dispatcher. It means there is no code written explicitly for
# this plugin, all the specifics are handled in this configuration
# and we call a simple command line client to perform the actual
# synthesis. Use this config file with the sd_generic output module.

# Debug turns debugging on or off
# See speechd.conf for information where debugging information is stored
Debug 0

# IMPORTANT: The audio output method relies on an audio playback
# utility (play, aplay, paplay for OSS, ALSA or Pulse)
# being installed. If this is not the case, consider installing it
# or replace the $PLAY_COMMAND string in the GenericExecuteString below
# with play, paplay or similar.
#
# GenericExecuteSynth is the shell command that should be
# executed in order to say some message. This command must
# stop saying the message on SIGKILL, otherwise it's useless.
# You can use the variables $LANGUAGE, $VOICE, $PITCH and $RATE
# which will be substituted for the appropriate value (you
# can modify this value, see other parameters).
# The command can be split into more lines, if necessary, using '\'.
GenericExecuteSynth \
"printf %s \'$DATA\' | espeak-ng -v mb-$VOICE -s $RATE -p $PITCH $PUNCT -q --stdin --pho | mbrola -v $VOLUME -e /usr/share/mbrola/$VOICE/$VOICE - -.au | $PLAY_COMMAND"

# Alternatively you can shorten the command like below, which makes it
# work directly with any audio playback utility, but then you won't
# be able to change the volume from the client application:
# GenericExecuteSynth \

GenericCmdDependency "mbrola"
